newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks open softer, Bre-X active.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks open softer, Bre-X active.

text.p: * Toronto stocks opened easier, pulling back after recent gains. * Bre-X topped actives. * Banks seen under pressure. * 16.6 million shares traded worth C$191.5 million.
Toronto stocks ticked lower at Wednesday's open, pulling back from recent gains as investors awaited the results of the U.S. 10-year bond auction at 1330 EDT (1730 GMT).
"We've had a pretty decent run. They're looking for an excuse to sell," one equities trader said. "It's extremely, extremely quiet."

Bre-X Minerals Ltd topped actives again after a report on Sunday that its Busang gold find was a fraud. "We're going to hear about Bre-X for a couple of weeks and then it'll disappear in the history books," another trader said.
Players are eyeing the US$12 billion 10-year bond auction at 1330 EST/1730 GMT.

This morning market watchers saw first quarter U.S. business productivity outside the farm sectior rise 2.0 percent on an annualized basis, short of the 2.4 percent gain expected by economists. However, March wholesale investories rose 0.7 percent compared to forecasts of 0.4 percent.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, only the gold group defied the landslide and rose. Consumer products, media and transportation led the weaker sectors.
The broader market was mixed, with winners outnumbering decliners 215 to 193 while 203 traded flat.
* Banks and their brokerages could remain under pressure as investors assess Bre-X losses and consider possible lawsuits, one trader said. The Bank of Montreal lost 0.30 to reach 51.60.
